title: Improving equilibrium propagation without weight symmetry through Jacobian homeostasis

en.text: To train a deep network, we almost reflexively reach for backpropagation. But backprop needs a separate linear backward pass and the exact transpose of every weight matrix, neither of which a physical neural system can naturally provide. Equilibrium Propagation (EP) is an appealing alternative: it is an energy-based method that estimates gradients from nothing more than the network's own relaxation toward equilibrium, which makes it a natural fit for physical substrates such as brains or analog and neuromorphic chips.

The catch is that classic EP rests on two demanding assumptions. First, the weights must be exactly symmetric, so that each forward connection equals its backward counterpart (w_ij equals w_ji). Second, the teaching nudge that pushes the network toward its target must be infinitesimally small. Both are hard to honor in real hardware. Worse, whether weight asymmetry actually hurts learning had never been pinned down, because its effect is always entangled with the error introduced by using a finite nudge and could not be observed on its own.

Why does this matter now? The answer is energy. Whether in a biological brain or a neuromorphic chip, physical neural systems could train networks at a small fraction of the energy that digital hardware spends. Yet the asymmetric version of EP had only ever worked on small tasks like MNIST, and it failed outright on CIFAR-10 for reasons nobody had explained. This ICLR 2024 paper, by Axel Laborieux and Friedemann Zenke, cleanly separates the two sources of bias and removes each in turn: finite-nudge bias is eliminated exactly with a Cauchy integral, and weight-asymmetry bias is tamed by a homeostatic loss that acts on the Jacobian. The payoff is that asymmetric networks train, for the first time, on ImageNet 32×32, with only a small gap to the ideal symmetric case.
Paper and code links: the arXiv paper is at https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02214 .
Background: why EP relies on symmetry, and why the bias was hard to study

EP works by letting the network relax to a free fixed point with no teaching signal, then applying a small nudge that pulls the output toward the target; comparing the two equilibria reveals the error each neuron should carry. The derivation hinges on the Jacobian at equilibrium being symmetric, because only then does the relaxation implicitly perform the transpose that backprop needs. Once the forward and backward weights are decoupled, the Jacobian picks up a skew-symmetric component, and the error direction read out from the dynamics drifts away from the true gradient.

en.caption: Figure 1. Three network types and their Jacobian after the free phase: a) an energy-based network with symmetric weights (w_ij equals w_ji) and a symmetric Jacobian; b) independent forward and backward connections, so the Jacobian is asymmetric; c) a feedforward network with a lower-triangular Jacobian. This paper targets the middle, asymmetric-with-feedback case.

en.text: In practice, though, that bias is hard to measure in isolation: as long as the nudge is finite, it introduces a bias of its own that masks the contribution of weight asymmetry. So "how much does asymmetry actually hurt" stayed an open, unexplained failure mode. The paper's first move is to pull these two sources apart analytically and handle each separately.
Method, part one: removing finite-nudge bias exactly with a Cauchy integral

The first bias comes from the finite nudge. The authors build on and extend holomorphic EP (hEP): they drive the network with a teaching signal that oscillates in the complex plane, β(t), and use a Cauchy integral from complex analysis to recover the exact derivative from the network's oscillatory response. What makes this elegant is that it returns an unbiased error estimate no matter how large the nudge and whether or not the Jacobian is symmetric. Better still, the integral can be estimated continuously over many oscillation cycles, so the network no longer has to alternate between a separate free phase and a nudged phase.

Reading the figure below, watch two things: how close each curve sits to the black dashed line (the true derivative), and how quickly it falls off as the teaching amplitude |β| grows. Classic EP, in grey, distorts rapidly once the nudge is large, whereas the Cauchy-integral estimate (hEP) hugs the true value even at large nudges. The two right-hand columns add that the error vector can even be read out online from the network's continuous oscillations, with no phase switching.

en.caption: Figure 2. Separating finite-nudge bias from Jacobian-asymmetry bias. a, b) Cosine similarity between the RBP error vector and those from classic EP (grey) and holomorphic EP (N=2 and N=10), as a function of the teaching amplitude |β|, for symmetric and non-symmetric Jacobians; classic EP diverges quickly from the true derivative (black dashed), while hEP stays close. c, d) Kernel density estimates of the cosine distribution in a two-hidden-layer MLP, worsening with asymmetry and depth. e, f) Continuous-time, online estimation of the free fixed point and the error vector from the oscillating signal.

en.text: Method, part two: shrinking Jacobian asymmetry with a homeostatic loss

The second bias comes from weight asymmetry. The authors first quantify it: the error's bias grows linearly with the skew-symmetric part A of the Jacobian, written d_β u* = δ − 2S⁻¹Aδ + o(·), where δ is the error vector we actually want and S is the symmetric part of the Jacobian. Since the bias is proportional to A, the natural move is to drive A down directly.

To that end they introduce a homeostatic loss that penalizes only the skew-symmetric part of the Jacobian, computed efficiently with the Hutchinson trace estimator and Gaussian noise, then added to the cross-entropy with a weight λ_homeo. Its form is L_homeo = E‖J_F ε‖² − εᵀ J_F² ε, with ε standard Gaussian noise. The key point is that this loss acts on the Jacobian, that is, on the network's functional symmetry, rather than forcing the weights themselves to be equal, so it applies even to architectures with no reciprocal connections at all.

The next figure confirms this from the angle of training dynamics. The top row trains with RBP (an approximation of backprop); the bottom row trains with hEP's exact error d_β u*. The contrast is telling: only the bottom row actively pulls the angle between forward and backward weights down over training (toward symmetry), and only there does the training loss depend on the initial angle; the top row barely changes the weight angle. This suggests that EP's own error signal nudges the network toward a more symmetric functional state.

en.caption: Figure 3. Training dynamics of a two-hidden-layer MLP on Fashion MNIST, with RBP on top and hEP's exact error d_β u* on the bottom. a, b) Evolution of the angle between forward and backward weights for different initial angles; training tends to reduce asymmetry. c, d) Learning curves; only hEP's training loss depends on the initial angle. e, f) Cosine similarity between the RBP and hEP error vectors over training.

en.text: Key result: the homeostatic loss brings asymmetric networks close to the symmetric ceiling

Put the two pieces together, removing nudge bias with the Cauchy integral and shrinking Jacobian asymmetry with the homeostatic loss, and the behavior of asymmetric networks changes qualitatively. The figure below tracks three different architectures during training (a reciprocally connected multi-layer network, a network whose output feeds directly back to the first layer, and the recurrent convolutional network used on CIFAR-10), reporting validation error, Jacobian symmetry, and layer-wise error alignment. The common pattern: with the homeostatic loss (dark red), Jacobian symmetry climbs steadily, hEP's error vectors align with RBP's layer by layer, and validation error drops accordingly. Read the rows top to bottom as a stress test: the same loss is asked to help three structurally different networks, and in each case the same story repeats.

en.caption: Figure 4. The homeostatic loss improves hEP training by acting directly on the Jacobian. Each row is an architecture–dataset pair: a–d) a reciprocally connected multi-layer network on Fashion MNIST, with validation error, Jacobian symmetry, and layer-wise error cosine; e–h) a network whose output feeds back to the first layer; i–l) the recurrent convolutional network on CIFAR-10, with validation error, weight angle, and layer-wise error cosine. Dark red adds the homeostatic loss; grey omits it.

en.text: The numbers make the case. On CIFAR-10, asymmetric hEP without the homeostatic loss reaches only 60.4% accuracy; add the loss and it jumps to 84.3%, just 4.3 points behind the fully symmetric architecture, all with only approximate weight symmetry. More importantly, this is the first time the method trains at all on ImageNet 32×32, reaching 31.4% Top-1 and 55.2% Top-5. The table below summarizes Top-1 accuracy for several variants across three datasets.

en.caption: Table 1. Top-1 validation accuracy (%) for asymmetric networks trained with hEP (ours) and RBP, averaged over three random seeds.

en.text: Ablation: how much each bias contributes

The ablations quantify each bias in turn. On Fashion MNIST, when the nudge is deliberately made large at |β|=0.5, classic one-sided EP falls apart and its error balloons to 38.4%; the six-point holomorphic estimate (N=6) brings it back to 14.3%, essentially matching the true derivative at 14.7%, which shows finite-nudge bias is fully removed. Separately, replacing the exact derivative with a coarse two-point estimate (N=2) costs about 2.9 points on CIFAR-10, and that gap is exactly the residual nudge bias. Meanwhile a network whose output feeds straight back to the first layer, with no reciprocal connections, benefits just as much, confirming that the loss targets functional symmetry rather than weight symmetry itself.
Takeaway and boundaries

The core message is that equilibrium propagation does not actually need perfectly symmetric weights. Remove finite-nudge bias exactly with a Cauchy integral, encourage functional symmetry of the Jacobian with a homeostatic loss, and asymmetric networks scale to ImageNet-level tasks with only a small gap to the ideal symmetric case. It is worth being honest about the boundary: a measurable gap to the symmetric ceiling remains, and the method adds the overhead of oscillatory estimation and the homeostatic term, both of which future work can refine.

Looking further out, functional symmetry is a much weaker and more attainable condition than weight symmetry. That points to a more biologically plausible route to training real physical substrates, and hints that the brain might rely on similar homeostatic mechanisms to learn effectively without ever making its connections exactly symmetric.

zh.text: 训练深度网络时，我们几乎默认要用反向传播（backpropagation）。但反向传播需要一条独立的线性反向通路，还要用到每个权重矩阵的精确转置，这在真实的物理神经系统里几乎无法实现。平衡传播（Equilibrium Propagation, EP）是一条颇具吸引力的替代路线：它属于基于能量的方法，只依靠网络自身朝平衡点弛豫的动力学来估计梯度，非常契合大脑或模拟／神经形态芯片这类物理载体。
问题在于，经典 EP 有两个近乎苛刻的前提。第一，权重必须严格对称，即前向连接与反向连接一一相等（w_ij 等于 w_ji）；第二，把网络推向目标的「nudge」教学信号必须无穷小。两者在真实硬件上都很难满足。更棘手的是，权重不对称到底会不会伤害学习，此前一直没有定论，因为它的影响总是和有限 nudge 带来的误差纠缠在一起，无法单独观察。

这为什么现在值得认真对待？答案是能耗。无论是生物大脑还是神经形态芯片，物理神经系统训练网络的能量成本都可能远低于数字硬件。而 EP 的非对称版本此前只在 MNIST 这类小任务上成功过，一到 CIFAR-10 就直接失败，且没人解释清楚原因。本文（ICLR 2024，作者 Axel Laborieux 与 Friedemann Zenke）把两类偏差干净地分开，并逐一消除：有限 nudge 偏差用一个 Cauchy 积分精确去除，权重不对称偏差则用一个作用在 Jacobian 上的「稳态损失」来抑制。结果是，非对称网络第一次被训练到了 ImageNet 32×32，且与理想对称情形只差很小一截。
论文与代码链接：arXiv 论文见 https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02214 。
背景：EP 为什么依赖对称，又为什么难分析
EP 的做法是让网络先在无教学信号时弛豫到一个「自由不动点」，再施加一个小 nudge 把输出往目标拉，比较两次平衡态，就能读出每个神经元应当承担的误差。这套推导成立的关键，是网络平衡点处的 Jacobian 对称——只有对称时，弛豫动力学隐含地完成了反向传播所需的转置操作。一旦前向与反向权重脱钩，Jacobian 就带上一个反对称分量，弛豫算出的误差方向随之偏离真正的梯度。

zh.caption: 图1 三类网络及其自由相后的 Jacobian：a）能量型网络权重对称（w_ij 等于 w_ji），Jacobian 对称；b）前向、反向连接独立，Jacobian 不对称；c）前馈网络的 Jacobian 为下三角。本文关注中间这种「有反馈但不对称」的情形。

zh.text: 但在实践中，这份偏差很难单独测量：只要 nudge 是有限大小，它本身就会引入另一种偏差，把权重不对称的贡献盖住。于是「非对称到底有多大害处」长期是一个悬而未决、也未被解释的失败模式。本文的第一步，就是把这两类来源在解析上彻底拆开，分别处理。
方法之一：用 Cauchy 积分精确消除有限 nudge 偏差

第一类偏差来自有限 nudge。作者沿用并推广了「全纯 EP（holomorphic EP, hEP）」的思路：把教学信号写成一个随时间振荡的复数信号 β(t)，再用复分析里的 Cauchy 积分，从网络的振荡响应里精确地把想要的导数还原出来。这一步的漂亮之处在于，无论 nudge 多大、也无论 Jacobian 是否对称，它都能给出无偏的误差估计；而且积分可以在多个振荡周期上连续估计，网络不必再切换「自由相」和「nudge 相」两个阶段。
读下面这张图时，可以先盯住两件事：一是曲线离黑色虚线（真实导数）有多近，二是它在教学幅度 |β| 变大时掉得有多快。灰色的经典 EP 一旦 nudge 变大就迅速失真，而 Cauchy 积分估计（hEP）即便在大 nudge 下也几乎贴着真值。右侧两栏进一步说明，这个误差向量甚至可以在网络的连续振荡中在线读出，无需分相。

zh.caption: 图2 分离有限 nudge 与 Jacobian 不对称两类偏差。a、b）在对称与非对称 Jacobian 下，RBP 误差向量与经典 EP（灰）、全纯 EP（N=2 与 N=10）所得误差向量的余弦相似度，随教学幅度 |β| 的变化；经典 EP 随 nudge 增大迅速偏离黑色虚线代表的真实导数，hEP 则一直贴近。c、d）两层 MLP 中余弦分布的核密度估计，随不对称与深度增加而变差。e、f）由振荡信号在连续时间中在线估计自由不动点与误差向量。

zh.text: 方法之二：用稳态损失直接压低 Jacobian 的不对称
第二类偏差来自权重不对称。作者先给出一个定量刻画：误差的偏差随 Jacobian 反对称分量 A 线性增长，写成 d_β u* = δ − 2S⁻¹Aδ + o(·)，其中 δ 是真正想要的误差向量，S 是 Jacobian 的对称部分。既然偏差正比于 A，一个自然的想法就是直接把 A 压小。

为此作者提出一个「稳态损失（homeostatic loss）」，它只惩罚 Jacobian 的反对称部分，可以用 Hutchinson 迹估计配合高斯噪声高效计算，再按系数 λ_homeo 加到交叉熵上一起训练。它的形式是 L_homeo = E‖J_F ε‖² − εᵀ J_F² ε（ε 为标准高斯噪声）。关键在于，这个损失作用在 Jacobian（也就是网络的「功能对称性」）上，而不是强行让权重本身相等——因此即使是完全没有互反连接的结构也同样适用。
下面这张图从训练动力学的角度验证了这一点。上排用 RBP（近似反向传播）训练，下排用 hEP 的精确误差 d_β u* 训练。值得对比的是：只有下排在训练中会主动让前向、反向权重的夹角变小（即向对称靠拢），而且训练损失对初始夹角敏感；上排则几乎不改变权重夹角。这说明 EP 的误差信号本身会推动网络走向更对称的功能状态。

zh.caption: 图3 两层 MLP 在 Fashion MNIST 上的训练动力学，上排用 RBP、下排用 hEP 的精确误差 d_β u*。a、b）不同初始夹角下前向与反向权重夹角的演化；训练倾向于减小不对称。c、d）学习曲线，只有 hEP 的训练损失依赖初始夹角。e、f）RBP 与 hEP 误差向量之间余弦相似度随训练的变化。

zh.text: 关键结果：稳态损失让非对称网络逼近对称上限

把两件事合起来——用 Cauchy 积分去掉 nudge 偏差、用稳态损失压低 Jacobian 不对称——非对称网络的表现发生了质变。下图给出三种不同结构（互反连接的多层网、输出直接回接首层的网、以及用于 CIFAR-10 的循环卷积网）在训练中的验证误差、Jacobian 对称度和逐层误差对齐度。共同的规律是：加了稳态损失（深红）后，Jacobian 对称度稳步上升，hEP 与 RBP 的误差向量逐层对齐，验证误差随之明显下降。

zh.caption: 图4 稳态损失通过直接作用于 Jacobian 改善 hEP 训练。每一行对应一种「结构—数据集」组合：a–d）互反连接的多层网在 Fashion MNIST 上的验证误差、Jacobian 对称度与逐层误差余弦；e–h）输出层直接回接首层的结构；i–l）用于 CIFAR-10 的循环卷积结构的验证误差、权重夹角与逐层误差余弦。深红为加入稳态损失，灰色为未加。

zh.text: 数字最能说明问题。在 CIFAR-10 上，不加稳态损失的非对称 hEP 只有 60.4% 的准确率；加入稳态损失后跃升到 84.3%，与完全对称的结构相比只差 4.3 个百分点，而这一切只需要近似的权重对称。更重要的是，这是该类方法第一次在 ImageNet 32×32 上训练成功，达到 31.4% 的 Top-1 与 55.2% 的 Top-5。下表汇总了几种变体在三个数据集上的 Top-1 准确率。

zh.caption: 表1 非对称网络用 hEP（本文）与 RBP 训练所得的 Top-1 验证准确率（%），三次随机种子平均。

zh.text: 消融：两类偏差各自贡献多少

消融实验把两类偏差的贡献分别量化。在 Fashion MNIST 上，当 nudge 被故意放大到 |β|=0.5 时，经典单边 EP 彻底崩掉，误差飙到 38.4%；换成六点的全纯估计（N=6），误差回到 14.3%，几乎等同于真实导数的 14.7%——这证明有限 nudge 偏差被完全消除。另一方面，把精确导数换成粗糙的两点估计（N=2），在 CIFAR-10 上会多付出约 2.9 个百分点，这部分正是残余的 nudge 偏差。而输出直接回接首层、完全没有互反连接的结构同样从稳态损失中获益，说明该损失针对的是功能对称性，而非权重对称性本身。
小结与边界
这篇论文给出的核心结论是：平衡传播其实并不需要严格对称的权重。只要用 Cauchy 积分精确消除有限 nudge 偏差，再用稳态损失去鼓励 Jacobian 的功能对称，非对称网络就能扩展到 ImageNet 级别的任务，且与理想对称情形只差很小一截。需要留意的是，与对称上限之间仍有可测量的差距，方法也引入了额外的振荡估计与稳态项开销，这些都是后续工作可以继续打磨的地方。
更长远地看，功能对称是一个比权重对称弱得多、也更容易实现的条件。这为在真实物理载体上训练神经网络提供了一条更具生物学合理性的路径，也隐约暗示：大脑或许正是依靠类似的稳态机制，在连接并不精确对称的前提下完成有效学习的。

en.title: Equilibrium Propagation Doesn't Need Symmetric Weights After All
en.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · Researchers at the Friedrich Miescher Institute and the University of Basel separate and remove the two biases that held equilibrium propagation back

这为什么现在值得认真对待？答案是能耗。无论是生物大脑还是神经形态芯片，物理神经系统训练网络的能量成本都可能远低于数字硬件。而 EP 的非对称版本此前只在 MNIST 这类小任务上成功过，一到 CIFAR-10 就直接失败，且没人解释清楚原因。本文（ICLR 2024，作者 Axel Laborieux 与 Friedemann Zenke）把两类偏差干净地分开，并逐一消除：有限 nudge 偏差用一个 Cauchy 积分精确去除，权重不对称偏差则用一个作用在 Jacobian 上的「稳态损失」来抑制。结果是，非对称网络第一次被训练到了 ImageNet 32×32，且与理想对称情形只差很小一截。
论文与代码链接：arXiv 论文见 https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02214 。

en.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · Researchers at the Friedrich Miescher Institute and the University of Basel separate and remove the two biases that held equilibrium propagation back

zh.title: 权重不必对称：Jacobian 稳态让平衡传播第一次跑上 ImageNet
zh.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · Friedrich Miescher 研究所与巴塞尔大学解耦并消除了平衡传播的两类梯度偏差

en.text: Background: why EP relies on symmetry, and why the bias was hard to study

EP works by letting the network relax to a free fixed point with no teaching signal, then applying a small nudge that pulls the output toward the target; comparing the two equilibria reveals the error each neuron should carry. The derivation hinges on the Jacobian at equilibrium being symmetric, because only then does the relaxation implicitly perform the transpose that backprop needs. Once the forward and backward weights are decoupled, the Jacobian picks up a skew-symmetric component, and the error direction read out from the dynamics drifts away from the true gradient.

en.caption: Figure 1. Three network types and their Jacobian after the free phase: a) an energy-based network with symmetric weights (w_ij equals w_ji) and a symmetric Jacobian; b) independent forward and backward connections, so the Jacobian is asymmetric; c) a feedforward network with a lower-triangular Jacobian. This paper targets the middle, asymmetric-with-feedback case.

en.text: In practice, though, that bias is hard to measure in isolation: as long as the nudge is finite, it introduces a bias of its own that masks the contribution of weight asymmetry. So "how much does asymmetry actually hurt" stayed an open, unexplained failure mode. The paper's first move is to pull these two sources apart analytically and handle each separately.

zh.text: 背景：EP 为什么依赖对称，又为什么难分析
EP 的做法是让网络先在无教学信号时弛豫到一个「自由不动点」，再施加一个小 nudge 把输出往目标拉，比较两次平衡态，就能读出每个神经元应当承担的误差。这套推导成立的关键，是网络平衡点处的 Jacobian 对称——只有对称时，弛豫动力学隐含地完成了反向传播所需的转置操作。一旦前向与反向权重脱钩，Jacobian 就带上一个反对称分量，弛豫算出的误差方向随之偏离真正的梯度。

zh.caption: 图1 三类网络及其自由相后的 Jacobian：a）能量型网络权重对称（w_ij 等于 w_ji），Jacobian 对称；b）前向、反向连接独立，Jacobian 不对称；c）前馈网络的 Jacobian 为下三角。本文关注中间这种「有反馈但不对称」的情形。

zh.text: 但在实践中，这份偏差很难单独测量：只要 nudge 是有限大小，它本身就会引入另一种偏差，把权重不对称的贡献盖住。于是「非对称到底有多大害处」长期是一个悬而未决、也未被解释的失败模式。本文的第一步，就是把这两类来源在解析上彻底拆开，分别处理。

zh.title: 权重不必对称：Jacobian 稳态让平衡传播第一次跑上 ImageNet
zh.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · Friedrich Miescher 研究所与巴塞尔大学解耦并消除了平衡传播的两类梯度偏差

en.caption: Figure 2. Separating finite-nudge bias from Jacobian-asymmetry bias. a, b) Cosine similarity between the RBP error vector and those from classic EP (grey) and holomorphic EP (N=2 and N=10), as a function of the teaching amplitude |β|, for symmetric and non-symmetric Jacobians; classic EP diverges quickly from the true derivative (black dashed), while hEP stays close. c, d) Kernel density estimates of the cosine distribution in a two-hidden-layer MLP, worsening with asymmetry and depth. e, f) Continuous-time, online estimation of the free fixed point and the error vector from the oscillating signal.

en.text: To train a deep network, we almost reflexively reach for backpropagation. But backprop needs a separate linear backward pass and the exact transpose of every weight matrix, neither of which a physical neural system can naturally provide. Equilibrium Propagation (EP) is an appealing alternative: it is an energy-based method that estimates gradients from nothing more than the network's own relaxation toward equilibrium, which makes it a natural fit for physical substrates such as brains or analog and neuromorphic chips.

The catch is that classic EP rests on two demanding assumptions. First, the weights must be exactly symmetric, so that each forward connection equals its backward counterpart (w_ij equals w_ji). Second, the teaching nudge that pushes the network toward its target must be infinitesimally small. Both are hard to honor in real hardware. Worse, whether weight asymmetry actually hurts learning had never been pinned down, because its effect is always entangled with the error introduced by using a finite nudge and could not be observed on its own.

Why does this matter now? The answer is energy. Whether in a biological brain or a neuromorphic chip, physical neural systems could train networks at a small fraction of the energy that digital hardware spends. Yet the asymmetric version of EP had only ever worked on small tasks like MNIST, and it failed outright on CIFAR-10 for reasons nobody had explained. This ICLR 2024 paper, by Axel Laborieux and Friedemann Zenke, cleanly separates the two sources of bias and removes each in turn: finite-nudge bias is eliminated exactly with a Cauchy integral, and weight-asymmetry bias is tamed by a homeostatic loss that acts on the Jacobian. The payoff is that asymmetric networks train, for the first time, on ImageNet 32×32, with only a small gap to the ideal symmetric case.
Paper and code links: the arXiv paper is at https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02214 .
Takeaway and boundaries

The core message is that equilibrium propagation does not actually need perfectly symmetric weights. Remove finite-nudge bias exactly with a Cauchy integral, encourage functional symmetry of the Jacobian with a homeostatic loss, and asymmetric networks scale to ImageNet-level tasks with only a small gap to the ideal symmetric case. It is worth being honest about the boundary: a measurable gap to the symmetric ceiling remains, and the method adds the overhead of oscillatory estimation and the homeostatic term, both of which future work can refine.

Looking further out, functional symmetry is a much weaker and more attainable condition than weight symmetry. That points to a more biologically plausible route to training real physical substrates, and hints that the brain might rely on similar homeostatic mechanisms to learn effectively without ever making its connections exactly symmetric.

方法之一：用 Cauchy 积分精确消除有限 nudge 偏差

第一类偏差来自有限 nudge。作者沿用并推广了「全纯 EP（holomorphic EP, hEP）」的思路：把教学信号写成一个随时间振荡的复数信号 β(t)，再用复分析里的 Cauchy 积分，从网络的振荡响应里精确地把想要的导数还原出来。这一步的漂亮之处在于，无论 nudge 多大、也无论 Jacobian 是否对称，它都能给出无偏的误差估计；而且积分可以在多个振荡周期上连续估计，网络不必再切换「自由相」和「nudge 相」两个阶段。
读下面这张图时，可以先盯住两件事：一是曲线离黑色虚线（真实导数）有多近，二是它在教学幅度 |β| 变大时掉得有多快。灰色的经典 EP 一旦 nudge 变大就迅速失真，而 Cauchy 积分估计（hEP）即便在大 nudge 下也几乎贴着真值。右侧两栏进一步说明，这个误差向量甚至可以在网络的连续振荡中在线读出，无需分相。

zh.caption: 图2 分离有限 nudge 与 Jacobian 不对称两类偏差。a、b）在对称与非对称 Jacobian 下，RBP 误差向量与经典 EP（灰）、全纯 EP（N=2 与 N=10）所得误差向量的余弦相似度，随教学幅度 |β| 的变化；经典 EP 随 nudge 增大迅速偏离黑色虚线代表的真实导数，hEP 则一直贴近。c、d）两层 MLP 中余弦分布的核密度估计，随不对称与深度增加而变差。e、f）由振荡信号在连续时间中在线估计自由不动点与误差向量。

en.title: Equilibrium Propagation Doesn't Need Symmetric Weights After All
en.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · Researchers at the Friedrich Miescher Institute and the University of Basel separate and remove the two biases that held equilibrium propagation back

zh.title: 权重不必对称：Jacobian 稳态让平衡传播第一次跑上 ImageNet
zh.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · Friedrich Miescher 研究所与巴塞尔大学解耦并消除了平衡传播的两类梯度偏差

en.text: Key result: the homeostatic loss brings asymmetric networks close to the symmetric ceiling

Put the two pieces together, removing nudge bias with the Cauchy integral and shrinking Jacobian asymmetry with the homeostatic loss, and the behavior of asymmetric networks changes qualitatively. The figure below tracks three different architectures during training (a reciprocally connected multi-layer network, a network whose output feeds directly back to the first layer, and the recurrent convolutional network used on CIFAR-10), reporting validation error, Jacobian symmetry, and layer-wise error alignment. The common pattern: with the homeostatic loss (dark red), Jacobian symmetry climbs steadily, hEP's error vectors align with RBP's layer by layer, and validation error drops accordingly. Read the rows top to bottom as a stress test: the same loss is asked to help three structurally different networks, and in each case the same story repeats.

en.caption: Figure 4. The homeostatic loss improves hEP training by acting directly on the Jacobian. Each row is an architecture–dataset pair: a–d) a reciprocally connected multi-layer network on Fashion MNIST, with validation error, Jacobian symmetry, and layer-wise error cosine; e–h) a network whose output feeds back to the first layer; i–l) the recurrent convolutional network on CIFAR-10, with validation error, weight angle, and layer-wise error cosine. Dark red adds the homeostatic loss; grey omits it.

en.text: The numbers make the case. On CIFAR-10, asymmetric hEP without the homeostatic loss reaches only 60.4% accuracy; add the loss and it jumps to 84.3%, just 4.3 points behind the fully symmetric architecture, all with only approximate weight symmetry. More importantly, this is the first time the method trains at all on ImageNet 32×32, reaching 31.4% Top-1 and 55.2% Top-5. The table below summarizes Top-1 accuracy for several variants across three datasets.

en.caption: Table 1. Top-1 validation accuracy (%) for asymmetric networks trained with hEP (ours) and RBP, averaged over three random seeds.

zh.text: 关键结果：稳态损失让非对称网络逼近对称上限

把两件事合起来——用 Cauchy 积分去掉 nudge 偏差、用稳态损失压低 Jacobian 不对称——非对称网络的表现发生了质变。下图给出三种不同结构（互反连接的多层网、输出直接回接首层的网、以及用于 CIFAR-10 的循环卷积网）在训练中的验证误差、Jacobian 对称度和逐层误差对齐度。共同的规律是：加了稳态损失（深红）后，Jacobian 对称度稳步上升，hEP 与 RBP 的误差向量逐层对齐，验证误差随之明显下降。

zh.caption: 图4 稳态损失通过直接作用于 Jacobian 改善 hEP 训练。每一行对应一种「结构—数据集」组合：a–d）互反连接的多层网在 Fashion MNIST 上的验证误差、Jacobian 对称度与逐层误差余弦；e–h）输出层直接回接首层的结构；i–l）用于 CIFAR-10 的循环卷积结构的验证误差、权重夹角与逐层误差余弦。深红为加入稳态损失，灰色为未加。

zh.text: 数字最能说明问题。在 CIFAR-10 上，不加稳态损失的非对称 hEP 只有 60.4% 的准确率；加入稳态损失后跃升到 84.3%，与完全对称的结构相比只差 4.3 个百分点，而这一切只需要近似的权重对称。更重要的是，这是该类方法第一次在 ImageNet 32×32 上训练成功，达到 31.4% 的 Top-1 与 55.2% 的 Top-5。下表汇总了几种变体在三个数据集上的 Top-1 准确率。

zh.caption: 表1 非对称网络用 hEP（本文）与 RBP 训练所得的 Top-1 验证准确率（%），三次随机种子平均。

把两件事合起来——用 Cauchy 积分去掉 nudge 偏差、用稳态损失压低 Jacobian 不对称——非对称网络的表现发生了质变。下图给出三种不同结构（互反连接的多层网、输出直接回接首层的网、以及用于 CIFAR-10 的循环卷积网）在训练中的验证误差、Jacobian 对称度和逐层误差对齐度。共同的规律是：加了稳态损失（深红）后，Jacobian 对称度稳步上升，hEP 与 RBP 的误差向量逐层对齐，验证误差随之明显下降。

zh.title: 权重不必对称：Jacobian 稳态让平衡传播第一次跑上 ImageNet
zh.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · Friedrich Miescher 研究所与巴塞尔大学解耦并消除了平衡传播的两类梯度偏差

en.caption: Figure 1. Three network types and their Jacobian after the free phase: a) an energy-based network with symmetric weights (w_ij equals w_ji) and a symmetric Jacobian; b) independent forward and backward connections, so the Jacobian is asymmetric; c) a feedforward network with a lower-triangular Jacobian. This paper targets the middle, asymmetric-with-feedback case.

en.text: To train a deep network, we almost reflexively reach for backpropagation. But backprop needs a separate linear backward pass and the exact transpose of every weight matrix, neither of which a physical neural system can naturally provide. Equilibrium Propagation (EP) is an appealing alternative: it is an energy-based method that estimates gradients from nothing more than the network's own relaxation toward equilibrium, which makes it a natural fit for physical substrates such as brains or analog and neuromorphic chips.

The catch is that classic EP rests on two demanding assumptions. First, the weights must be exactly symmetric, so that each forward connection equals its backward counterpart (w_ij equals w_ji). Second, the teaching nudge that pushes the network toward its target must be infinitesimally small. Both are hard to honor in real hardware. Worse, whether weight asymmetry actually hurts learning had never been pinned down, because its effect is always entangled with the error introduced by using a finite nudge and could not be observed on its own.

Why does this matter now? The answer is energy. Whether in a biological brain or a neuromorphic chip, physical neural systems could train networks at a small fraction of the energy that digital hardware spends. Yet the asymmetric version of EP had only ever worked on small tasks like MNIST, and it failed outright on CIFAR-10 for reasons nobody had explained. This ICLR 2024 paper, by Axel Laborieux and Friedemann Zenke, cleanly separates the two sources of bias and removes each in turn: finite-nudge bias is eliminated exactly with a Cauchy integral, and weight-asymmetry bias is tamed by a homeostatic loss that acts on the Jacobian. The payoff is that asymmetric networks train, for the first time, on ImageNet 32×32, with only a small gap to the ideal symmetric case.
Paper and code links: the arXiv paper is at https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02214 .

zh.caption: 图1 三类网络及其自由相后的 Jacobian：a）能量型网络权重对称（w_ij 等于 w_ji），Jacobian 对称；b）前向、反向连接独立，Jacobian 不对称；c）前馈网络的 Jacobian 为下三角。本文关注中间这种「有反馈但不对称」的情形。

zh.text: 训练深度网络时，我们几乎默认要用反向传播（backpropagation）。但反向传播需要一条独立的线性反向通路，还要用到每个权重矩阵的精确转置，这在真实的物理神经系统里几乎无法实现。平衡传播（Equilibrium Propagation, EP）是一条颇具吸引力的替代路线：它属于基于能量的方法，只依靠网络自身朝平衡点弛豫的动力学来估计梯度，非常契合大脑或模拟／神经形态芯片这类物理载体。
问题在于，经典 EP 有两个近乎苛刻的前提。第一，权重必须严格对称，即前向连接与反向连接一一相等（w_ij 等于 w_ji）；第二，把网络推向目标的「nudge」教学信号必须无穷小。两者在真实硬件上都很难满足。更棘手的是，权重不对称到底会不会伤害学习，此前一直没有定论，因为它的影响总是和有限 nudge 带来的误差纠缠在一起，无法单独观察。

这为什么现在值得认真对待？答案是能耗。无论是生物大脑还是神经形态芯片，物理神经系统训练网络的能量成本都可能远低于数字硬件。而 EP 的非对称版本此前只在 MNIST 这类小任务上成功过，一到 CIFAR-10 就直接失败，且没人解释清楚原因。本文（ICLR 2024，作者 Axel Laborieux 与 Friedemann Zenke）把两类偏差干净地分开，并逐一消除：有限 nudge 偏差用一个 Cauchy 积分精确去除，权重不对称偏差则用一个作用在 Jacobian 上的「稳态损失」来抑制。结果是，非对称网络第一次被训练到了 ImageNet 32×32，且与理想对称情形只差很小一截。

en.text: Key result: the homeostatic loss brings asymmetric networks close to the symmetric ceiling

Put the two pieces together, removing nudge bias with the Cauchy integral and shrinking Jacobian asymmetry with the homeostatic loss, and the behavior of asymmetric networks changes qualitatively. The figure below tracks three different architectures during training (a reciprocally connected multi-layer network, a network whose output feeds directly back to the first layer, and the recurrent convolutional network used on CIFAR-10), reporting validation error, Jacobian symmetry, and layer-wise error alignment. The common pattern: with the homeostatic loss (dark red), Jacobian symmetry climbs steadily, hEP's error vectors align with RBP's layer by layer, and validation error drops accordingly. Read the rows top to bottom as a stress test: the same loss is asked to help three structurally different networks, and in each case the same story repeats.

en.caption: Figure 4. The homeostatic loss improves hEP training by acting directly on the Jacobian. Each row is an architecture–dataset pair: a–d) a reciprocally connected multi-layer network on Fashion MNIST, with validation error, Jacobian symmetry, and layer-wise error cosine; e–h) a network whose output feeds back to the first layer; i–l) the recurrent convolutional network on CIFAR-10, with validation error, weight angle, and layer-wise error cosine. Dark red adds the homeostatic loss; grey omits it.

More importantly, this is the first time the method trains at all on ImageNet 32×32, reaching 31.4% Top-1 and 55.2% Top-5. en.title: Equilibrium Propagation Doesn't Need Symmetric Weights After All
en.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · Researchers at the Friedrich Miescher Institute and the University of Basel separate and remove the two biases that held equilibrium propagation back

zh.title: 权重不必对称：Jacobian 稳态让平衡传播第一次跑上 ImageNet
zh.subtitle: ICLR 2024 · Friedrich Miescher 研究所与巴塞尔大学解耦并消除了平衡传播的两类梯度偏差

en.text: Background: why EP relies on symmetry, and why the bias was hard to study

EP works by letting the network relax to a free fixed point with no teaching signal, then applying a small nudge that pulls the output toward the target; comparing the two equilibria reveals the error each neuron should carry. The derivation hinges on the Jacobian at equilibrium being symmetric, because only then does the relaxation implicitly perform the transpose that backprop needs. Once the forward and backward weights are decoupled, the Jacobian picks up a skew-symmetric component, and the error direction read out from the dynamics drifts away from the true gradient.

en.caption: Figure 1. Three network types and their Jacobian after the free phase: a) an energy-based network with symmetric weights (w_ij equals w_ji) and a symmetric Jacobian; b) independent forward and backward connections, so the Jacobian is asymmetric; c) a feedforward network with a lower-triangular Jacobian. This paper targets the middle, asymmetric-with-feedback case.

en.text: In practice, though, that bias is hard to measure in isolation: as long as the nudge is finite, it introduces a bias of its own that masks the contribution of weight asymmetry. So "how much does asymmetry actually hurt" stayed an open, unexplained failure mode. The paper's first move is to pull these two sources apart analytically and handle each separately.
Takeaway and boundaries

The core message is that equilibrium propagation does not actually need perfectly symmetric weights. Remove finite-nudge bias exactly with a Cauchy integral, encourage functional symmetry of the Jacobian with a homeostatic loss, and asymmetric networks scale to ImageNet-level tasks with only a small gap to the ideal symmetric case. It is worth being honest about the boundary: a measurable gap to the symmetric ceiling remains, and the method adds the overhead of oscillatory estimation and the homeostatic term, both of which future work can refine.

Looking further out, functional symmetry is a much weaker and more attainable condition than weight symmetry. That points to a more biologically plausible route to training real physical substrates, and hints that the brain might rely on similar homeostatic mechanisms to learn effectively without ever making its connections exactly symmetric.

zh.caption: 图1 三类网络及其自由相后的 Jacobian：a）能量型网络权重对称（w_ij 等于 w_ji），Jacobian 对称；b）前向、反向连接独立，Jacobian 不对称；c）前馈网络的 Jacobian 为下三角。本文关注中间这种「有反馈但不对称」的情形。

zh.text: 小结与边界
这篇论文给出的核心结论是：平衡传播其实并不需要严格对称的权重。只要用 Cauchy 积分精确消除有限 nudge 偏差，再用稳态损失去鼓励 Jacobian 的功能对称，非对称网络就能扩展到 ImageNet 级别的任务，且与理想对称情形只差很小一截。需要留意的是，与对称上限之间仍有可测量的差距，方法也引入了额外的振荡估计与稳态项开销，这些都是后续工作可以继续打磨的地方。
更长远地看，功能对称是一个比权重对称弱得多、也更容易实现的条件。这为在真实物理载体上训练神经网络提供了一条更具生物学合理性的路径，也隐约暗示：大脑或许正是依靠类似的稳态机制，在连接并不精确对称的前提下完成有效学习的。
